background_story: Dr. Michael Jenkins was a renowned entomologist with a passion for the most obscure insects. His colleagues often joked that he had a knack for finding the most elusive creatures. Michael's fascination with the Cryptocercidae family, commonly known as wood cockroaches, led him to spend years studying their behavior and habitats. His groundbreaking research on the social structure of these ancient insects earned him international recognition. Michael's dedication to his work took him to remote forests, where he spent months observing and collecting specimens. His discoveries shed new light on the evolution of social insects and earned him the nickname 'The Cockroach Whisperer' among his peers.
